title: Spend-throttle region and SKU fallback with spot-burst limits
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: We need a routing policy that enforces soft and hard spend caps per-customer and per-route while still maximizing throughput and respecting latency SLOs. Current region/tier selection is deterministic and prefers cheaper spot SKUs aggressively; customers with bursty traffic sometimes exceed budget targets and experience instability when spot is suddenly evicted. This ticket proposes a "spend-throttle" middleware that combines a leaky-bucket budget window with a dynamic SKU-region preference score and a controlled spot-burst allowance.
design_summary: High-level design: (1) Maintain a rolling spend-window (user-route granularity) with token accounting (tokens represent allowed spend units). (2) Preference score = weighted sum of [cost_delta, latency_penalty, eviction_risk, reserved_capacity_headroom]. (3) Routing chooses the highest-preference compatible endpoint while ensuring tokens remain. (4) Spot-burst: allow short-lived temporary spot allocations even if tokens are low, bounded by a burst_quota and guarded by an eviction-mitigation timer. (5) Fallback rules: when tokens exhausted or eviction risk high, automatically degrade to on-demand/reserved SKUs or to smaller model variant and record a structured reasons log for observability.
tradeoffs: Accuracy vs cost: preferring cheaper SKUs reduces cost but increases eviction complexity; this design accepts limited short bursts to preserve quality for low-latency requests.
Complexity vs observability: token accounting needs new metrics but gives precise spend control; we add explicit telemetry to minimize debugging burden.
Per-customer fairness: aggressive global spillover limits are required to prevent noisy neighbors; we use per-tenant windows to isolate impact.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Core accounting service - implement per-tenant, per-route leaky-bucket with configurable window and token-cost mapping.
Phase 2: Runtime preference function - surface eviction_risk and reserved_headroom from scheduler, implement scoring and tie-breakers.
Phase 3: Spot-burst controller - add burst_quota, burst_cooldown, and eviction-mitigation heuristic (graceful KV-cache save + fast warmup options).
Phase 4: Fallback orchestration - controlled model-size downgrade and on-demand route promotion with observable reasons and runbook.
Phase 5: Canary rollout - 1% traffic -> 10% -> 25% with automated metric gates (cost, error-rate, median latency).
metrics_and_gates: primary: spend_per_tenant_per_minute (should stay within configured soft cap +/- 10%)
slo: P50 latency increase <= 10% for promoted on-demand paths
quality: model-output regression rate (as measured by eval prompts) stays < 1%
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant soft and hard spend caps are persistently enforced in the accounting service.
Routing respects preference scores and never routes to a candidate when its use would violate a hard cap.
Spot-burst behavior allows temporary bursts but honors burst_quota and cooldown; documented by tests.
Rollout can be reverted via feature flag without requiring infra changes.
Dashboards show spend tokens, preference score distribution, and fallback reason histograms for customers in canary.
test_strategy: Unit tests for token accounting under concurrent consumption patterns.
Integration test: simulated eviction events to verify eviction-mitigation path and observed KB/caching behavior.
Load test: spike traffic patterns to validate burst_quota and cooldown behavior under 10k rps.
Canary monitoring: synthetic transactions with deterministic prompts to detect quality regressions immediately.
rollout_plan: Deploy accounting service + feature flag behind edge: off by default.
Enable for internal customers and infra-facing traffic for 48h, evaluate metrics.
Open canary 1% external traffic for 72h; if gates pass => 10% for 48h => 25% for 72h.
Full enable only after two consecutive successful cycles and stakeholder signoff.
